text:
sam.support: Customer escalation — multiple customers reporting SSE streams abruptly stop mid-response when routed via Cloudflare -> ALB -> our nginx origin. Cuts off consistently at ~34s. Ticket links: #CS-5273, #CS-5301.

ashley.eng: Can you paste quick repro steps and an example curl? Also which ALB settings and Cloudflare plan?

sam.support: Repro I used locally with a staging domain behind Cloudflare (Free), ALB in front of EC2 w/ nginx. Curl: 
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://staging-stream.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test"
```
Observed: initial SSE event(s) stream for ~1-2s then silence; connection stays open from client perspective but no further chunks arrive. After ~34s, connection resets with TLS close.

mike.netops: Checked ALB access logs for the staging host — target_response_time shows a spike then connection termination. Target kept reporting 200 but bytes_sent stops increasing. ALB idle timeout is default 60s. Cloudflare edge reports upstream idle after 35s on a few requests.

jordan.sre: Hypothesis: Cloudflare edge uses its own proxy timeouts and may cut or reset an idle HTTP/2 stream earlier than ALB expects, or an intermediate GOAWAY/reset from ALB/Envoy to origin causes multiplexed stream loss. Also nginx proxy buffering could be holding chunks until buffer fills, producing a long silence then a burst or termination.

ashley.eng: Here's the minimal nginx snippet we used on origin: 
```
server {
  location /v1/stream {
    proxy_pass http://app_upstream;
    proxy_buffering off;   # we set this during tests
    proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
  }
}
```
We tried with and without proxy_buffering. With buffering on, the client saw larger pauses. With buffering off, it behaved better, but still hit the ~34s cutoff when Cloudflare was enabled.

mike.netops: ALB->target connection closed logs show FIN from ALB after a small window when Cloudflare edge re-sent a PROBE or HTTP/2 SETTINGS that we didn't handle gracefully. Not all runs reproduce. I also saw nginx error.log entries: 
```
[error] 12345#0: *789 writev() failed (32: Broken pipe) while sending to client, client: 10.0.0.2, server: staging, request: "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1"
```

sam.support: Customers are seeing this in prod intermittently—one reported partial completion of generated text and an automatic reconnect with truncated context. That breaks many LLM flows.

jordan.sre: Short-term mitigations: (1) Disable HTTP/2 on the ALB listener so CF -> ALB uses HTTP/1.1 (avoids stream multiplexing GOAWAY resets), (2) set Cloudflare to pass-through (disable HTTP/2 or use a worker to force keep-alive headers), (3) ensure nginx has `proxy_buffering off` for the SSE route and `sendfile off;` to avoid kernel-level buffering quirks. Also consider increasing ALB idle timeout to 120s to avoid ALB-triggered closes.

ashley.eng: Additional workaround we tested — add explicit SSE comment pings every 15s from the origin (": ping

") so edges see continuous data. That made CF keep the stream open. Not ideal but helps until infra fix.

dev-bot: trace: route=/v1/stream -> runtime/model-x -> kvcache (prefix enabled) -> sse-flusher interval=0s -> last-flush=0.5s

mike.netops: Action items: I'll spin up a reproducible stack (CF Free + ALB + nginx) and toggle ALB HTTP/2 + idle timeout, collect pcap and ALB logs. If CF is the culprit, we can document the CF setting for customers.

ashley.eng: I'll try a server-side change: ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and emit small chunks frequently, and test with CF HTTP/2 disabled. Will report back in a few hours.

jordan.sre: For long-term fix, eng-runtime should add explicit SSE flush hooks that emit 1-2 byte keepalive events and detect midstream disconnects to checkpoint tokens so reconnects can resume with less loss. Assigning to eng-runtime backlog.

sam.support: Thanks — keeping this open. Labeling as Escalation / streaming / proxy-timeouts. We'll update customers with the workaround (ping every 15s or disable HTTP/2 on ALB/CF) until root cause is fixed.
